feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform expertise. It reads professionally and is well aligned to strategy/content roles, but it would be stronger with tighter formatting consistency, a few grammar fixes, and more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing advancement from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ internal publishers, and broad analytics stack.  
- Well-positioned brand for digital strategy, web modernization, advocacy communications, and cross-functional leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact/results: include % growth, engagement gains, cost savings, process improvements, campaign outcomes, or team/budget size to increase impact.  
- Fix writing/grammar consistency: “more than 12 years experience” should be “more than 12 years of experience”; add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lines); standardize hyphenation such as “organization-wide” and “member-facing.”  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate overlapping sections to improve structure and scannability.  

Typos/misspellings: no obvious misspellings found. Minor style issue: “Coleman DAVIS” in all caps for surname may feel inconsistent unless used intentionally throughout.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding public-sector/advocacy relevance would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Add sector context: public-sector, membership, or mission-driven organizations to align with the NACo experience.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “multi-channel digital communications” to reduce listiness.
- Emphasize leadership outcomes and modernization focus in one concise value statement.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, web and platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed capabilities listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad or generic phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform governance & CMS management.”
- Reduce overlap by focusing on strategic competencies, not tools or execution details already covered in Topline Skills/Technical + IT.
- Improve parallel structure and consistency: use noun phrases throughout and standardize style (e.g., “cross-functional stakeholder coordination” instead of “stakeholder & cross-department coordination”).
- Possible rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS management • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Content operations & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant duplication with Header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, advocacy messaging, analytics, multimedia, and coordination.
- “Workflow design” and “systems architecture” are close enough that they may read as repetitive.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting-level outcomes, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper consulting summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and cross-channel governance for member-facing communications.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets and emphasize outcomes: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and publishing systems that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet more concise: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Elevate the most distinctive work: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX for complex policy content.” Add metrics if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording repeats governance, analytics, and digital operations already covered in “Director of Digital Media.”
- Microsite and AI-search details also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level unless you add measurable results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 impact bullets, e.g.:
- “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia production.”
- “Expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and channel decision-making.”
- “Established digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and operational efficiency.”
- If possible, add outcomes for email/social/video: growth %, engagement lift, cost savings, production volume, or turnaround reduction.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with Associate Communications Director; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Governance/workflow language also appears in the current consulting role; differentiate by emphasizing team leadership and platform modernization here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize scope, operational leadership, and channel-building contributions that set up the Director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector membership audience.”
- Combine bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders, improving consistency and cadence across core email communications.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable policy communications channel.”
- Rephrase internal-process bullets to show leadership: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning with communications, advocacy and program staff, and standardized publishing workflows to improve coordination and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep focus here on establishing the channel at scale.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 Director entry; avoid similar wording like “strengthened digital operations.”

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing standards & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for a more current, integrated feel.
- Swap “messaging” for “communications” or “campaigns” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows, align wording to proven strengths from recent roles: Drupal modernization, governance, analytics-informed planning, AI-enabled discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat almost verbatim from Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is vague and partially covered by campaign/storytelling language in recent experience and projects.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work, not every platform detail.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items unless they are job-target critical: remove “jQuery” and consider removing “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” from this topline line.
- Put the strongest recent differentiators first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Drupal modernization for large public-facing sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- Most platform/tool names repeat the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make this more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability statement: “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than just platforms.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace weaker phrases with impact-oriented ones: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance analysis and optimization,” “SEO insights.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive reporting and dashboarding • SEO, UX and digital performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization” section; keep Topline Skills focused on strategic capabilities, and leave the full tool inventory in Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker and less specific than “executive reporting and dashboarding.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent digital leader, this item should emphasize strongest/current platforms and reduce lower-signal entries.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance and recency: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project; it feels less strategic than the rest.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either “CMS Platforms” or “Web Platforms & CMS” across sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- If both sections stay, use this item for platforms only and keep modernization/AI/search/integrations in the Topline Skills section.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation strengths that support recent work rather than basic coding terms alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge scripting with Cloudflare Workers • Deployment automation with GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value at this level.
- Consider adding scope/outcome context if format allows: “used for Drupal microsites, analytics instrumentation, and workflow automation.”
- If accurate, replace generic “API integrations” with examples tied to recent work, e.g. “CMS, analytics, and campaign platform integrations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation.”
- GTM may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you specifically use it for implementation-heavy tagging architecture.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since workflow automation already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize categories and strongest tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana • Slack/Teams • Trello/Basecamp”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application: “workflow automation, project coordination, and cross-team collaboration tools”
- Prioritize tools tied to recent work and technical depth; keep Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams
- Consider dropping older/lower-signal tools like Basecamp or Trello unless they were materially used in recent roles

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” is already stated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating that phrase elsewhere without adding specificity
- Airtable systems and workflow automation also appear under Web Platforms & Technical Execution, so this section should stay concise rather than restate capability claims

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and under-leverages your recent leadership in email operations. It should signal platform depth and align more clearly with the NACo work on newsletters, audience communications, and coordinated digital campaigns.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/context rather than just listing tools, e.g.: **Higher Logic (newsletter and member communications) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (campaign automation) • Mailchimp**
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one platform to measurable use: newsletters reaching **tens of thousands** or support for **multi-channel campaign communications**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and recent NACo roles.
- If these platforms were not hands-on in recent roles, don’t overstate them; keep the list ordered by actual depth of use.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” production volume, or workflow improvements from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Split into concrete contributions: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; helped improve publishing workflows and cross-channel coordination.”
- Make outputs more specific: “Contributed to a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social output, or size/scope of the website refresh; clarify supervisory scope (“mentored 1 digital media associate”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version framed as launching/building the format, not scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; use earlier-stage wording like “helped formalize” or “supported initial build-out.”

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, research, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to lead with the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while expanding the organization’s early digital storytelling capacity.”
- Make the podcast achievement more concrete: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” into clearer ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy-focused initiatives.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership; keep this positioned as a coordinator role with one notable first-launch achievement.
